Hi Priya / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side and a suggested next step to kick off the 4-week POC so we can validate model selection and confirm latency/cost tradeoffs.

Recap (short):
- Goal: Integrate LLM into Acme's customer support routing and canned-response generation.
- Key success criteria you called out: 90%+ intent routing precision, average generation latency < 600ms p95, and acceptable multilingual quality for ES/PT.
- Data: You agreed to share a ~2k-row sample of historical support messages plus an intent label column.

Suggested POC scope (proposed):
1) Week 0/1: Ingest sample_eval_set.csv, run baseline prompts against 2 open models.
2) Week 2: Evaluate accuracy + quality; iterate prompts and caching.
3) Week 3: Run quantized inference profiles, measure p95 latency and cost.
4) Week 4: Produce final report, recommend production model and routing/fallback policy.

Proposed model candidates for trial (initial suggestion):
- Primary: Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized q4o) — balance of quality and cost for English + fine-tuning/prompting.
- Fallback: Llama-2-7b-chat — lower-cost variant for low-latency fallback routes.
- Multilingual experiments: Mistral-7B-Instruct and BLOOMZ variants for Spanish/Portuguese checks.

Ownership / asks from Acme:
- Please upload sample_eval_set.csv to the Drive link I shared (or reply with a secure transfer).
- Confirm target SLOs and any strict PII/redaction rules we need to respect.

Attachments: POC_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (draft) and sample_eval_set.csv (template).

Next steps:

- Languages: primary is English, but we need reliable support for Spanish (ES) and Portuguese (PT). If the multilingual models lag, acceptable fallback is English-first + translated responses, but quality must be > 85% judged by our bilingual reviewers.

Subject: Re: POC Trial: Model selection & success criteria - SE plan + next steps

Hi all, thanks for the clear brief. Confirming SE ownership (I'll lead the POC) and here's a concise plan we can execute during the 4-week window.

POC objective: validate model selection (quality, latency, cost) and a fallback routing policy that meets Acme's accuracy and latency SLOs, including bilingual performance for ES/PT.

Evaluation plan (baseline -> optimize):
- Inputs: sample_eval_set.csv (2k rows), heldout bilingual review set (~200 rows) for human quality checks.
- Metrics: intent routing precision/recall, top-1 accuracy for canned responses, bilingual human-quality score (1-5), p95 latency under synthetic 50-concurrent load, and tokens-per-request cost.
- Benchmarks (pass/fail): intent precision >= 0.90, p95 latency <= 600ms (target), bilingual quality >= 4/5 average.

Model candidates to run in parallel (initial):
1) Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized q4o) — Primary candidate for English-heavy traffic.
2) Llama-2-7b-chat (quantized q4o) — Lower-cost fallback for routing when latency/cost constraints hit.
3) Mistral-7B-Instruct — better multilingual generalization for ES/PT; include one run to gauge quality.
4) BLOOMZ-3B (or BLOOMZ-7B if needed) — optional multilingual check if Mistral underperforms on PT.

Fallback & routing policy suggestion:
- Route to primary (13B) by default. If p95 or cost thresholds breached, shift lower-priority traffic to 7B fallback. For ES/PT: prefer Mistral route for those languages; if Mistral latency > 800ms, fall back to 7B + translation pass (English-first).

Perf / quantization profile to test:
- q4o and q4_k_mixed on 13B (compare throughput and quality delta).
- q4o on 7B (baseline).

Timeline & milestones:
- Week 0 (kickoff, access): ingest sample_eval_set.csv, confirm Drive access and HubSpot deal link.
- Week 1: run baseline inference across the 4 model candidates on a 200-row subset; collect initial metrics.
- Week 2: full-run on 2k set + bilingual holdout; mid-POC checkpoint call to review metrics and decide tuning steps.
- Week 3: prompt optimization, caching/kv prefix tuning, quantized runs to measure p95/cost.
- Week 4: final runs, produce report with recommended model, routing policy, and estimated monthly cost at projected traffic.

Ownership & contacts:
- Redwood SE lead: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.com) — technical lead and run owner.
- Redwood AE: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com) — commercial & timeline owner.
- Acme reviewers: Priya Rao, Alex Chen — will provide bilingual review and acceptance.

Kickoff: Confirming Wednesday 26 Aug at 11:00am PT works for me — I will send a calendar invite and include the Drive + HubSpot links.

Next steps for Acme:
- Upload sample_eval_set.csv to the Drive link.
- Share any compliance constraints (retention / redaction) and a contact for SRE if we need dedicated VLAN or Private deployment testing.

I've attached an updated POC_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf with a week-by-week checklist. I'll also seed the Drive folder with a short test harness we use to run evaluation scripts.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.
